section_summary: Pages 149-158 conclude a Portuguese-language promotional pamphlet presenting Japan as a resilient and rapidly advancing industrial, commercial, and maritime power, with particular attention to cotton textiles, heavy industry, wartime finance, shipping, and economic relations with Brazil. The pamphlet defends Japanese policy in China, contrasts Japanese ambitions with British and American power, and advertises the São Paulo office of a Japanese trade or industrial federation. Pages 159-160 are filing and cross-reference notes pointing to reports on Japanese activities and propaganda in São Paulo, including a proposed Japanese-government-sponsored visit by University of São Paulo professors.

subfiles.title: Portuguese-language promotional pamphlet on modern industrial Japan (conclusion)
subfiles.from: Federação Industrial do Japão / Japan Foreign Trade Federation
subfiles.about: The concluding portion promotes Japan's economic strength, industrial growth, shipping capacity, and commercial relationship with Brazil.
subfiles.summary: The pamphlet describes falling Japanese cotton-textile exports while emphasizing Japan's continuing importance as a market for raw cotton. It praises the expansion of heavy and chemical industries, rejects predictions of Japanese financial collapse during the war in China, and celebrates the growth of the merchant marine. A polemical section compares Japanese policy in China with British imperialism and argues that conflict arises between established and rising powers. The closing pages promote Japan-Brazil trade and invite readers to obtain information from the federation's São Paulo office.

subfiles.about: The note directs researchers to a despatch transmitting Carol H. Foster's report on Japanese activities in São Paulo state.
subfiles.summary: File note cross-referencing a despatch on Japanese activities in Sao Paulo transmitting a report by Carol Foster; OCR obscures details.

subfiles.about: The note cross-references a report on Japanese propaganda in São Paulo and a planned visit to Japan by University of São Paulo professors.
